title: Article 146 — Officers and servants and the expenses of the Supreme Court

content.overview: Article 146 provides that appointments of officers and servants of the Supreme Court shall be made by the Chief Justice of India or such other Judge or officer of the Court as the Chief Justice may direct, subject to any law by Parliament and to rules under this article. Subject to parliamentary law, conditions of service of officers and servants are prescribed by rules made by the Chief Justice or his directed authority, with Presidential approval for rules relating to salaries, allowances, leave or pensions. Administrative expenses of the Supreme Court, including salaries, allowances and pensions, are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.
content.glance: SC staff appointed by CJI (or directed Judge/officer). Service conditions by rules (Presidential approval for pay/leave/pension rules). Expenses charged on Consolidated Fund of India.
content.study:
Article 146 protects the institutional independence of the Supreme Court in staffing and finances:
- Appointments by CJI or directed Judge/officer.
- Conditions of service by rules (Presidential approval for specified financial rules).
- Administrative expenses charged on the Consolidated Fund of India (not subject to annual vote in the same way as ordinary expenditure).

Examination: CJI control of appointments; charged expenditure; Presidential approval for certain rules.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Appointments of officers and servants: by CJI or directed Judge/officer.
2. Conditions of service: rules (Presidential approval for salaries, allowances, leave, pensions).
3. Administrative expenses charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How are officers and expenses of the Supreme Court provided for under Article 146?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 146, appointments of officers and servants of the Supreme Court are made by the Chief Justice of India or such other Judge or officer as the Chief Justice may direct. Conditions of service are prescribed by rules, with the approval of the President required for rules relating to salaries, allowances, leave or pensions. The administrative expenses of the Supreme Court, including salaries, allowances and pensions payable to officers and servants of the Court, are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.

examTips: CJI appoints staff; expenses charged on Consolidated Fund.

keyTakeaways: Art 146: SC staff and charged expenses; institutional independence.
